hook: Set aside a long evening: this is a novella-length file assembled from recovered messages, exploration videos and a stack of debriefings, with its own navigation menu at the top. The ruined complex at its center carries Foundation markings, yet the Foundation's own records say it was never built. Hold on to the title question, because the article answers it in full only at the very end.
whyItMatters: 1730 is one of the wiki's big multi-team exploration epics, sending several task forces into the same ruin across years of in-universe time. It is also a major piece of alternate-history Foundation fiction, imagining what the organization turns into once it loses its independence and its ethics are bent toward someone else's agenda. Readers following Tau-5 "Samsara" or Bobble the Clown will find both here, used in ways that feed into their wider stories.
thingsToNotice: The first half is fragments: scrawled warnings, a doomed team's final log, and memos that treat cruelty as routine paperwork. The second half becomes a rescue mission, and the calm, almost cheerful Tau-5 operatives set against the worn-down human squads give it a strange rhythm. Dr. Hadley's letter and Dr. Scott's debrief explain the Thresher machine from two sides, one driven by revenge and one by fear. Captain Hollis frames the whole file, vanishing near the start and making the final choice at the machine, and the crater left behind is the answer to where Site-13 goes next.

related.note: Another vision of the Foundation turned into something monstrous.
Another descent into a Foundation site from a reality that went wrong.
